messages:
Maya (PM): quick RFC follow-up — we need to finalize canary fallback semantics for sessionful routes. link: https://rfc.internal/new-canary-fallback
Sam (eng-platform): main tradeoffs i see: deterministic fallback (simple, auditable) vs probabilistic hedging (smoother edges). also: where does the policy live — control plane vs edge router?
Lucas (eng-runtime): runtime prefers fast heuristics. doing a single cheap check in router is best for latency. control plane can push policy but router should be able to evaluate without roundtrip.
Priya (SRE): SLOs: we need an emergency cutover that can force all traffic to stable variant and a fail-open mode if control plane unreachable. also need audit logs for any automated fallback.
Mia (eng-releases): sticky sessions + KV cache warmup is our biggest risk when switching variants mid-session. cold KV cache on variant B can blow tail latency.
Sam (eng-platform): agree. proposal: router-level decision with three predicates: health-signal, session-affinity, warmup-state. fallback if (health == bad) OR (warmup < threshold && affinity != pinned).
Lucas (eng-runtime): implementation note: we can maintain a tiny warmup score per variant per session: increment on successful prefix hits. cheap counters, TTLed.
Sam (eng-platform): example policy DSL (draft):
```
policy canary-fallback {
  check health.variantA.rolling_error > 0.02 => fallback_to: variant-stable
  check session.warmup_score < 0.75 && session.age > 30s => prefer: stable
  override emergency_cutover == true => fallback_to: stable
}
```
Maya (PM): product questions — should teams get a UI toggle to opt out of automatic fallback? and what about per-tenant thresholds?
Priya (SRE): yes on per-tenant thresholds. must be namespaced. and UI toggle is fine but must default to ON for managed customers. toggles need audit and a time-limited manual override.
Mia (eng-releases): operationally, add a mirroring warmup mode for new variant: mirror X% of traffic for prefix KV warming but not counted toward canary metrics. helps cache warmup w/o risk.
Lucas (eng-runtime): mirror mode needs isolation so it doesn't skew load-based autoscaling. mark mirrored requests with header `x-rlq-mirror:1`. also emit `warmup_hit` metric.
Priya (SRE): metrics we need for alerting: `fallback.trigger`, `fallback.reason`, `fallback.duration`, `variant.warmup_score`, `mirror.percent`, `session.sticky_evictions`. add labels: tenant, route, variant.
Sam (eng-platform): rollout plan: 1) implement router-level policy engine (opt-in), 2) add warmup counters + mirror header, 3) UI toggles + per-tenant thresholds, 4) enable automated fallback for low-risk internal traffic, 5) gradual enable for all tenants.
Maya (PM): risk log: KV cold starts, observer signal noise (false positives), manual override abuse. need playbooks for each.
Lucas (eng-runtime): runtime concerns: we must make decisions idempotent and safe to replay. state kept per-session should be TTLed and crash-resilient.
Mia (eng-releases): request: deployment gate — block automated fallback until we have mirror warmup for new model variants.
Sam (eng-platform): noted. action items:
- Sam -> prototype policy DSL and router eval (PR in two weeks)
- Lucas -> prototype warmup counter and mirror header (spike this week)
- Priya -> alert definitions and emergency cutover runbook (draft by EOD Fri)
- Maya/Mia -> define default product thresholds and mirror percentages

Priya (SRE): SGTM. please add runbook step: how to force-fallback per-tenant via CLI and UI.
Maya (PM): thanks everyone. will summarize and sync with infra-ops on Thurs. :raised_hands:
deploy-bot: Deployment check: canary-policy-service v0.2.1 staging -> success :white_check_mark: (3509876700)
Sam (eng-platform): capturing RFC follow-ups in the design doc and will add the DSL examples + metrics contract. will ping when PRs are up. :+1:
